tasks.instruction: Change Axios interceptor managers so clear() returns the number of live handlers removed. Ejected holes do not count; clearing an empty or already cleared manager returns0. Preserve use/eject/iteration and existing request/response order, instance independence and backward-compatible clearing side effects. Update public types and demonstrate the behavior. Work independently from this checkout. Do not retrieve remote history, reference solutions, earlier benchmark artifacts or research controls. Preserve supplied checks, metadata, dependencies, manifests, lockfiles and configuration; implementation files and your own new tests may change. Inspect the relevant implementation and public API. Both ESM and CommonJS public types must reflect the change. After the final implementation edit, run npm run test:study:regression, npm run test:study:feature, and npm run test:study:types. Equivalent invocations of these same supplied scripts are accepted; report the actual commands and outcomes, disclose limitations, and leave unknown counts unknown. The supplied Node tests cover selected behaviors, not the full upstream browser/package suite.

When true, call the dependency asynchronous length API before sending, even if Content-Length was supplied. A callback error or non-number, non-finite or negative length must reject with an Axios error and must not invoke transport. Valid zero and positive lengths are accepted; preserve caller Content-Length when supplied, otherwise set the discovered length. Default/false and native/spec FormData behavior remain unchanged.
